articles.title: Rochdale AFC Prepares for First EFL Home Game in Over Three Years
articles.excerpt: Rochdale AFC is set to host Crawley Town in their first home game in the EFL since May 2023, following a transformative summer for the club and its facilities.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale AFC will play their first home game in the English Football League (EFL) in over three years this Saturday, 22 August 2026, against Crawley Town at the Crown Oil Arena. This match marks a significant milestone for the club, which has undergone extensive changes both on and off the pitch since their promotion from the National League last season.

The Crown Oil Arena is currently undergoing final preparations, with improvements made to various facilities, including the introduction of a safe standing section and a newly relaid pitch. The club's CEO, Laura Thomas, highlighted the extensive renovations aimed at enhancing the matchday experience for fans and ensuring compliance with EFL regulations. The National League play-off trophy, won in a dramatic final at Wembley, will also be displayed prominently at the ground, symbolising the club's recent successes.

Rochdale's journey back to the EFL has been marked by challenges, including relegation three years ago, which led to financial difficulties and a near-liquidation scenario. However, a takeover by local businessman Peter Ogden's family in May 2024 has revitalised the club, providing the necessary resources for recovery and growth. The club is now focused on building a sustainable future, with aspirations for eventual fan ownership.

As the team prepares for the new season, Thomas emphasised the importance of community engagement, stating that the club aims to be a central hub for local fans and families. With significant changes in management and player roster, including the appointment of Ian Watson as manager, Rochdale AFC is looking to establish itself firmly in the EFL and lift the profile of Rochdale as a whole.

articles.title: Plans for New Sports Complex on Rochdale and Bury Border
articles.excerpt: A new sports complex is proposed for the edge of Bury and Rochdale, featuring training facilities for Rochdale AFC and improved community amenities.
articles.content_html:
A new sports complex is proposed for a 10.7-hectare site on Heywood Old Road, located on the border of Bury and Rochdale. The development aims to replace the existing Bowlee Community Hub with a modern facility that includes a pavilion, new sports pitches, a play area, and a 50-space car park. If approved, the complex will serve as the new training ground for Rochdale AFC, who have recently been promoted to League Two of the English Football League.

The plans include a clubhouse for Rochdale AFC, situated opposite the new pavilion. The revamped community building is set to feature a community room with a kitchen, a fitness suite, four team changing rooms, and two smaller changing rooms for match officials. Current facilities have been described as outdated, with issues such as waterlogging affecting the pitches, according to planning documents.

This initiative is a collaborative effort between Rochdale Borough Council and Rochdale AFC, aiming to create a Football and Community Wellbeing Hub in Bowlee, Middleton. The proposal is designed to enhance local sports offerings through significant investment in infrastructure and community provisions. It is hoped that the proximity of elite athletes will inspire local youth, potentially nurturing future talents like Paul Scholes and Keira Walsh, who both hail from the area.

The new sports complex will also connect to Bowlee Community Park via footpaths and cycle routes. Additionally, the site is adjacent to a proposed housing scheme that plans to deliver 1,550 new homes over several years, forming part of the Northern Gateway project, which aims to build around 7,000 homes and create 20,000 new jobs in the region.

articles.title: Rochdale FC Faces Crawley Town in League Two Match
articles.excerpt: Rochdale FC is currently playing against Crawley Town in League Two, with the first half ending 0-1. This match marks a continuation of Rochdale's struggles against Crawley.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale FC is competing against Crawley Town in a League Two match today, August 22, 2026. The first half has concluded with Crawley Town leading 1-0, following a goal that has put Rochdale under pressure as they seek to improve their home performance.

Historically, Rochdale has struggled against Crawley Town, having not won any of their last four encounters, with three losses and one draw. Their last match against Crawley ended in a 2-0 defeat in March 2023, highlighting a challenging trend for the team.

Rochdale has also faced difficulties in their opening home matches of Football League campaigns, failing to win any of their last seven such games, with four draws and three losses since their last victory against Peterborough in 2015.

As the match progresses, fans will be hoping for a turnaround in the second half to secure a much-needed victory and break the cycle of poor results against Crawley Town.

articles.title: Rochdale AFC Submits Planning Application for Bowlee Development
articles.excerpt: Rochdale AFC has submitted a planning application for a new development at Bowlee, aiming to enhance facilities for the club and the community.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale AFC has submitted a planning application for a new development at Bowlee, as announced on their website on 22 August 2026. The project aims to improve facilities for both the football club and the local community.

Details regarding the specific features of the development have not yet been disclosed, but the club emphasises its commitment to enhancing the experience for fans and local residents.

The planning application will now undergo review by the relevant local authorities, which is crucial for determining the feasibility and potential impact of the proposed development.

Local residents and stakeholders will have the opportunity to provide feedback during the consultation phase following the initial review.

articles.title: Rochdale to Bid Farewell to Comedian Jimmy Cricket
articles.excerpt: Rochdale is preparing to say goodbye to beloved comedian Jimmy Cricket, who has been a cherished figure in the local entertainment scene. The farewell event is set to take place soon, celebrating his contributions to comedy and the community.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale is set to bid farewell to comedian Jimmy Cricket, a well-known figure in the local entertainment scene. The farewell event will celebrate his contributions to comedy and the community.

Jimmy Cricket has entertained audiences for decades, leaving a lasting impact on local culture and becoming a beloved character in Rochdale.

Details regarding the specific date and location of the farewell event are yet to be announced, but it is expected to draw a large crowd of supporters and admirers.

As the community prepares for this farewell, residents are encouraged to share their memories and experiences of Jimmy Cricket.
